reasoning_traces.think:
The core reasoning process is modeled as a triadic relationship: S (reality), M (mental abstraction), and P (inferred property). The selection of M is governed by the subjective interest in P, such that M is chosen to mediate inference from S to P. This is formalized as a conditional probability P(P|S,M) ∝ P(S|M)P(M), where M acts as a latent variable. When P is deemed important (I > threshold), M is optimal; otherwise, an alternative M' is preferred. Cognitive selection is a dynamic process where M is updated based on W (world context), leading to state transitions S → M → P. The failure mode occurs when I misaligns with actual causal structure, or when M is no longer representative of S under new W. The duality lies in the interplay between subjective interest and objective structure, where reasoning is both a tool of cognition and a reflection of embedded values.
